source: NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1, 10 m wind, long-term monthly means 1991-2020 (NOAA PSL), T62 Gaussian grid (192 x 94, ~1.9 deg) bilinearly interpolated to 1 deg
height: 10 m above the surface (land and sea)
citation: Kalnay, E. et al. (1996). The NCEP/NCAR 40-Year Reanalysis Project. Bull. Amer. Meteor. Soc. 77, 437-471, doi:10.1175/1520-0477(1996)077<0437:TNYRP>2.0.CO;2. NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1 data provided by the NOAA PSL, Boulder, Colorado, USA, from their website at https://psl.noaa.gov
licence: NOAA PSL / NCEP data: public, no restrictions on use (US Government work); acknowledge as cited
attribution: Winds: NCEP/NCAR Reanalysis 1, 1991-2020 monthly means (NOAA PSL)
annual_note: annual = vector mean of the 12 monthly means
caveats: A monthly-mean wind is the vector average: where the wind changes direction (monsoons, the ITCZ, storm tracks) the mean is much weaker than typical winds on any day; mean speed of the instantaneous wind is higher.
Reanalysis at ~1.9 deg: coastal jets, gap winds and tropical cyclones are smoothed out.
Winds over land are included (it is a global field); mask them in the viewer if only the ocean is wanted.

grid.registration: cell centres; row 0 = northernmost, column 0 = westernmost from 180 W; longitudes wrap
grid.encoding: zlib-deflated; u then v, each little-endian int16 stored as two byte planes (all low bytes, then all high bytes); value (m/s) = q * scale; q = -32768 = no data
grid.components: u = eastward, v = northward (true north, not grid north)
